newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebels close in on Zaire's second city.
newsitem.headline: Rebels close in on Zaire's second city.

text.p: The forces of rebel leader Laurent Kabila closed in on Zaire's second city on Monday, taking the town of Kipushi just 30 km (20 miles) away and advancing along the road towards Lubumbashi itself.
Lubumbashi appeared to be effectively encircled, leaving no clear avenue of escape for Zaire government troops and elite presidential guard units recently sent to reinforce them.
The city was calm but shops and major businesses were closed, including the headquarters of the Gecamines mining company and Sizarail, a Belgian-South African consortium which runs local railways.
Zaire airlines cancelled all flights to Lubumbashi and a scheduled flight from Johannesburg was put on hold.
Surprised residents in Kipushi, which lies hard by the Zambian border to the southwest of Lubumbashi, said by telephone the rebel force had entered the town from the direction of the southern border.
"There were perhaps one to two thousand of them. They were armed and in uniform and mostly young," said businessman Gilbert Mbangu, speaking by telephone from his home in Kipushi.
He said the rebels entered the town in the early morning, meeting no resistance, and headed on to Lubumbashi at dawn on foot.
Government troops had melted away and there had been no violence or looting in Kipushi, Mbangu said.
In Lubumbashi, businesses with contacts in Kipushi confirmed the rebels had swept through the town taking residents completely by surprise.

Mbangu said the force appeared to have come from the direction of the Zambian border post near Kipushi, but it was unclear whether they had come in from Zambia itself or emerged from the bush on the Zairean side of the frontier.
Unconfirmed reports in the past few days said the rebels were encircling Lubumbashi, including a movement of forces from east to west on the south side of the city.
The governor of Zaire's mineral-rich Shaba province, Kyungu wa Kumwanza, told reporters he had no details about Kipushi.
But he once again urged that there should be no bloodshed or looting in Lubumbashi, a message some locals take as a coded signal to the rebels that there will be no resistance.
